title: Questions to ask a wedding venue before you book
seo_title: Questions to ask a wedding venue before you book
dek: The questions that matter at every viewing, from what the price includes to music curfews, suppliers, access and cancellation, wherever in the world you marry.
body:
A venue viewing is the one meeting where the venue is selling and you are buying, and that balance shifts the moment you sign. The questions below are the ones worth asking while it is still in your favour. They work for a country house in England, a rooftop in New York, a hotel ballroom in Dubai or a farmhouse outside Florence, because the things that cause problems later are much the same everywhere: what is included, what is restricted, what happens on the day and what happens if plans change.

Take this list to every viewing, write the answers down and ask the venue to confirm the important ones in writing. A friendly coordinator who says "that won't be a problem" is not the same as a clause in a contract.

## Availability, dates and exclusivity

Start here, because nothing else matters if the date does not work.

- **Which dates are free in your season, and how quickly are they going?** If you are flexible, ask which days of the week and which months are easiest to book. Friday, Sunday and weekday weddings are often quieter, and quieter can mean more choice.
- **Is the venue exclusive to you for the day?** Some venues host more than one wedding or event on the same day, in different rooms or at different times. Ask who else will be on site and whether any spaces, entrances or car parks are shared.
- **What time can you get in, and what time must everyone be out?** Ask about access the day before for setting up, and the time suppliers must have packed everything away.
- **Is there a hold on the date while you decide?** Ask how long a provisional booking lasts and whether anyone else can overtake it.

Popular months differ by country, so do not assume your local peak is everyone's. Official figures show August was the most popular month for weddings in England and Wales in 2023, and for opposite-sex couples in Ireland in 2024, while Australia's busiest single date in 2024 fell in February. The [Roko report on what official statistics say about when and how people marry](/journal/weddings-by-the-numbers-what-official-statistics-show) sets the figures side by side.

## What the price includes

Two quotes that look alike can describe very different days. Ask for a written breakdown and go through it line by line.

- **What exactly is included in the hire fee?** Tables, chairs, linen, crockery, glassware, staff, a dance floor, a ceremony room, a bridal suite and cleaning are sometimes included and sometimes charged separately.
- **Is there a minimum spend or a minimum number of guests?** Many venues set a minimum on food and drink, especially for Saturdays and peak months. Ask what happens if your final numbers fall below it.
- **Which taxes and service charges are added, and are they in the quoted figure?** In some countries tax and gratuity are added on top; in others they are already included.
- **What costs extra on the day?** Corkage, cake cutting, late-night food, overtime for staff, security and extended hours are the usual extras.
- **Can you see the price for your exact date and numbers?** A brochure price for a winter weekday is not the price of a summer Saturday.

If you are working with a modest budget, ask which packages the venue offers for smaller weddings, off-peak days or shorter hire periods. The best venues are often happy to talk about this, and it is much easier to negotiate before you book than after.

## Food, drink and suppliers

This is where restrictions usually hide.

- **Must you use the venue's own caterer, or can you bring your own?** If you can bring your own, ask whether caterers need to come from an approved list and whether the venue charges a kitchen fee.
- **Can you supply your own drinks?** Ask about corkage per bottle, whether there is a bar minimum and whether the bar can stay open until the end.
- **Do suppliers need to be approved or insured?** Some venues ask for public liability insurance and risk assessments from every supplier. Find out early so your photographer, band and florist can send what is needed.
- **Can the kitchen handle the menu you want?** If your wedding needs a particular cuisine, such as Indian, kosher, halal or a full vegan menu, ask whether the kitchen has done it before and whether an outside specialist can work alongside the venue's team.
- **Are there tastings, and are they included?**

## Ceremony and legal requirements

Whether a venue can host your legal ceremony depends on the law where you marry, not on the venue's wishes.

- **Is the venue licensed or approved for legal ceremonies?** In some countries, including England and Wales, civil ceremonies must take place in approved premises. Elsewhere, a celebrant or officiant can marry you almost anywhere. Check the rules for the country you are marrying in, with the relevant government or registration office.
- **Where would the ceremony take place, and what is the wet-weather plan?** If the ceremony is outdoors, ask to see the indoor alternative and how quickly the room can be turned around.
- **Are there rules about music, readings, candles or religious elements?** Some venues restrict open flames, confetti or amplified music during the ceremony.
- **For a religious or cultural ceremony, is there space for everything it needs?** A mandap, a chuppah, a tea ceremony or a long procession all need room, time and sometimes extra permissions.

## Music, noise and the end of the night

- **What time must music stop?** Many venues have a licence or neighbour agreement that sets a hard finish.
- **Is there a sound limiter?** If there is, ask your band or DJ to speak to the venue before you book them.
- **Where can the band or DJ set up, and how much power is available?**
- **Are fireworks, sparklers, sky lanterns or a late-night bonfire allowed?**

## Guests, access and accommodation

- **How many guests can you seat for dinner, and how many can attend in the evening?** The ceremony room, the dining room and the evening space often have different capacities.
- **Is the venue accessible for every guest?** Ask about step-free routes, accessible toilets, parking close to the entrance and quiet spaces for anyone who needs a break.
- **Are there bedrooms on site, and do you have to book them all?** Some venues include rooms; others require you to take every room for exclusive use.
- **How do guests get there and get home?** Ask about parking, taxis, late-night transport and the nearest hotels.
- **Are children welcome, and are there any restrictions on where they can go?**

## The coordinator and the day itself

- **Who will be your contact during planning, and who will be in charge on the day?** These are not always the same person.
- **How many staff will be working at your wedding?** Ask about the ratio of serving staff to guests for the meal.
- **Can you have a final meeting and a walk-through before the day?**
- **What happens if something goes wrong?** Ask about back-up power, a wet-weather plan and first aid.

## Contracts, payments and cancellation

Read the contract slowly before you pay anything.

- **What is the deposit, when are the remaining payments due and are they refundable?**
- **What happens if you need to move the date or cancel?** Ask how much you would lose at each stage and whether the venue will try to resell the date.
- **What happens if the venue has to cancel?** Ask what they would refund and whether they would help find an alternative.
- **Can the prices change between booking and the wedding?** Ask whether the quote is fixed or whether food, drink and staffing can rise.
- **Does the venue recommend wedding insurance, and does it hold its own?**

Ask for every promise made at the viewing to appear in the contract, including the date, the times, the spaces, the guest numbers, the inclusions and the price.

## After the viewing

Compare venues on what the day will actually cost and how it will actually run, not on the brochure. Put your answers side by side, add up the real total for your numbers and note anything that would rule a venue out.

When you are ready to shortlist, you can [browse event and wedding businesses on Roko](/wedding-vendors), compare their details and contact them directly. Once the venue is booked, the same questions about inclusions, insurance and cancellation are worth asking of every other supplier you hire.

faq.q: How many wedding venues should you view?
faq.a: View enough to compare like with like. Shortlist on date, capacity and budget first, then visit the venues that pass, with the same list of questions for each, so you can compare the answers side by side.

faq.q: Should you get venue promises in writing?
faq.a: Yes. Ask for the date, times, spaces, guest numbers, inclusions and price to appear in the contract, along with anything the coordinator agreed at the viewing, such as access times or permission for your own drinks.

faq.q: What is a minimum spend at a wedding venue?
faq.a: It is an amount you agree to spend on food and drink, or on the hire as a whole, regardless of your final guest numbers. Ask what the minimum is for your date and what happens if your numbers fall below it.

faq.q: Can any venue host a legal wedding ceremony?
faq.a: It depends on the law where you marry. In some countries, including England and Wales, civil ceremonies must take place in approved premises, while elsewhere a celebrant can marry you almost anywhere. Check with the government or registration office for the country you are marrying in.
